assessment.summary: Type design concerns — The loader promises a validated Config while returning unchecked JSON whose endpoint cannot be a URL instance.

positives.summary: Configuration parsing is localized behind one exported boundary.

findings.title: Unchecked configuration boundary
findings.summary: loadConfig asserts arbitrary JSON to Config even though JSON parsing cannot construct the declared URL instance.
findings.whyItMatters: A public TypeScript return type should describe the runtime value the boundary actually constructs. Callers receive a string while the compiler permits URL methods, and malformed retry values flow into arithmetic as trusted numbers.
findings.impact: Callers receive a string while the compiler permits URL methods, and malformed retry values flow into arithmetic as trusted numbers.

evidence.message: Config declares endpoint as a runtime URL object.

findings.recommendation: Parse into unknown, validate the primitive fields, and construct URL before returning Config. Boundary validation adds code, but it centralizes conversion and lets downstream code rely on the exported contract.

opinion.summary: I would address the unchecked configuration boundary before merging.
